why: B: on every abstract connected Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with any smooth Mathlib RiemannianBundle metric and any Levi-Civita connection, Milnor-complete, simply connected, ⟨R(A,B)A,B⟩ ≤ 0, for all p, q: the blind Ω(M; p, q) (d-ball topology) is connected; it is homotopy equivalent to a Hausdorff Mathlib CWComplex with no cells of positive dimension whose l-cells correspond to the geodesics (in Ω*) of blind index l (GeodIdx, index = bIndex of the variational HessT); and every connected Hausdorff CW complex with only 0-cells is a point. A (universes 0): for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with the induced metric only: Theorem 17.3 with all indices 0 for closed N (the project's IsCountableCellComplexType, not a Mathlib CWComplex), geodesics = points of the fibre exp_p⁻¹(q), Ω* ≃ₕ fibre, fibre discrete and countable with Ω ≃ₕ fibre, contractibility of Ω for complete simply connected N, and a one-cell structure for closed simply connected N. A ⇒ B fails genuinely (abstract manifolds are not given embedded); B ⇒ A fails genuinely (setting; B has nothing on exp-fibres or the project's cell-complex notion, and covers only the simply connected case). On embedded manifolds A ⇒ B_emb and B_emb ⇒ A's contractibility statement are both proved.
